- When sentiment is negative in the recent history, reduce forecasted values by 2–5% to account for downward pressure.  
- If model shows a sharp upward spike (e.g., >10% above recent mean), apply a 5–10% downward correction to prevent over-optimism.  
- If forecast mean is consistently above true outcome over 3–5 days, apply a 3–7% downward bias to align with mean reversion.  
- When sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish signals, reduce forecast volatility and favor smoother, trend-following adjustments.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows early sharp decline (first 5–7 days), adjust forecast downward by 3–8% to reflect early correction.  
- If sentiment history includes multiple negative signals (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative values), apply a 5–10% downward bias to the entire forecast horizon.
